tq: Trace the source-to-exposure pathway instead of focusing only on the name of the gas.

s: Radon exposure in enclosed spaces is particularly significant because radon is regarded as:
o: A harmless gas unless mixed with oxygen
A leading cause of lung cancer after smoking
The main cause of radiation burns in nuclear workers
The leading cause of skin cancer after ultraviolet radiation
x: Radon accumulation in closed rooms is a major health concern because it is a leading cause of lung cancer after smoking.
tq: Distinguish the specific health outcome and rank stated for the hazard.

Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Natural source or material)
A. Cosmic rays
B. Radon
C. NORM

List-II (Associated description)
1. Naturally occurring radioactive materials such as uranium, thorium, radium and potassium-40 in rocks and water
2. Radioactive noble gas from the Earth's crust

Select the correct answer using the code given below.

s:
Which of the following are recognised man-made sources of radioactive pollution?
1. Accidents at nuclear plants such as Chernobyl and Fukushima
2. Fallout from weapons testing containing Sr-90, Cs-137 and I-131
3. Mining and refining of uranium and thorium, including tailings
4. Improper disposal of medical and industrial radioactive sources

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: All four are identified man-made sources of radioactive pollution. Reactor waste is also a man-made source, although it is not separately included in the statements.
tq: Use the source classification and recognise that several listed human activities can be simultaneously correct.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a natural source or naturally occurring radioactive material?
o: Fallout containing strontium-90 from weapons testing
Potassium-40 present in rocks and water
x: Weapons-test fallout containing strontium-90 is a man-made source. Cosmic rays, radon and naturally occurring potassium-40 are natural sources or materials.
tq: Classify each option as natural or man-made and identify the exception.

s: Which one of the following combinations correctly represents possible effects of radioactive pollution?
o: Only temporary fatigue and increased soil fertility
Reduction of radiation intensity and rapid soil renewal
Improved crop growth and permanent immunity to cancer
Cancer, leukaemia, genetic mutation and radiation burns
x: Radioactive pollution can cause cancer, leukaemia, genetic mutations and radiation burns. It can also leave soil infertile for decades.
tq: Select the option containing the complete set of stated adverse effects without an unsupported benefit.

s: The harmful effect of radiation depends primarily upon:
o: Intensity of radiation, exposure time and half-life
The distance of the source from the equator alone
The colour and physical state of the radioactive material alone
Whether the radiation is produced naturally, irrespective of dose
x: The harm caused by radiation depends on its intensity, the duration of exposure and the half-life of the radioactive material.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding institutional responsibilities:
1. The AERB approves the handling and disposal of radioactive waste.
2. The Environmental Survey Laboratory monitors radiation around nuclear plants.
3. The Environmental Survey Laboratory approves all radioactive waste disposal sites.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
